result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both tables right-align two-decimal amounts in tabular figures, use one unambiguous date style, separate rows with hairlines, and keep currency consistent. B is better because each status pairs the word with a distinct symbol (check, triangle, dashed circle), while A repeats the same dot and leans on color. Overdue stays clear in both without a loud row fill: A reddens the due date and uses a pale pill, and B uses a red triangle and label. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A edges ahead because each status pairs the word with a different mark—a check, a triangle, or an open circle—while amounts stay decimal-aligned under one USD header. Both tables use an unambiguous month-name date, light row rules, and a quiet overdue treatment. B is equally consistent on currency and decimals, but every status uses the same dot, so color does more of the distinction.
